QuestionStmt.S: A metal sphere cools at a rate of $1.5^\circ C/\text{min}$ when its temperature is $80^\circ C$. When the temperature of the sphere is $40^\circ C$ its rate of cooling is $0.3^\circ C/\text{min}$. The temperature of the surrounding ($\theta_0$) is

Solution.S:
According to Newton's law of cooling: $\left|\frac{dT}{dt}\right| = k(T - \theta_0)$.

At $T = 80^\circ C$, $1.5 = k(80 - \theta_0)$ ... (i)

At $T = 40^\circ C$, $0.3 = k(40 - \theta_0)$ ... (ii)

Dividing (i) by (ii): $\frac{1.5}{0.3} = \frac{80 - \theta_0}{40 - \theta_0} \Rightarrow 5 = \frac{80 - \theta_0}{40 - \theta_0}$.

Cross-multiply: $5(40 - \theta_0) = 80 - \theta_0 \Rightarrow 200 - 5\theta_0 = 80 - \theta_0 \Rightarrow 120 = 4\theta_0 \Rightarrow \theta_0 = 30^\circ C$.

Thus the correct option is A: $30^\circ C$.
